notfallblatt.einleitung: Keep this sheet safe – printed in a safe place or in a password safe, separate from the device running Ablago. Whoever has it can read your backups. Without the key no backup can be restored.
notfallblatt.schluessel.hinweis: Upper and lower case count, the spaces between the groups don’t. The zero is crossed out. Below characters that are easily confused it says which one is meant.
notfallblatt.fingerabdruck.hinweis: Ablago uses it when restoring to check whether the key fits.
notfallblatt.ablage.sicherungen.text: are in the backup folder of this installation.
notfallblatt.ablage.sicherungen.aussen: are in the backup folder of this installation and as an off-site copy: {ziele}.
notfallblatt.ablage.aufrufe.text: These addresses accept calls (automations, only with a signature): {liste}. Switch off under Workbench → Automations.
notfallblatt.ablage.aussen.warnung: User and password for the off-site copy are deliberately not here. The key isn’t at the destination – never put it there.
notfallblatt.fragen.leer: Who helps you in an emergency? Enter name and phone:
notfallblatt.fragen.seite2: Your emergency contacts are on page 2.
notfallkontakte.text: People you trust who should be asked in an emergency – someone from the family, for example. They get no account and no access. Ablago sends them a short info email without a link, and they appear on the emergency sheet under “Whom to ask?”.
notfallkontakte.name: Name
notfallkontakte.notiz.hinweis: Appears on the emergency sheet, never in the email – e.g. “my brother, helped with the setup”.
notfallkontakte.antwort.hinweis: Otherwise your address is not in the email. Only the person who added the contact can switch it on.
notfallkontakte.erneut.heute: Already sent again today – possible again tomorrow.
notfallkontakte.loeschen.text: {name} will be removed. If they received the info email, a short notice follows.
notfallkontakte.mail.offen: Info email will be sent as soon as email is set up
notfallkontakte.mail.wartet: Info email is waiting to be sent
notfallkontakte.max: At most {max} emergency contacts – delete one to add a new one.
notfallkontakte.blatt-neu: The emergency contacts have changed: print the emergency sheet again.
notfallkontakte.ohne-versand: Email sending is not set up yet. The info emails go out as soon as it is.
notfallkontakte.ergebnis.offen: Saved. The info email will be sent as soon as email is set up.
notfallkontakte.ergebnis.fehler: Saved, but the info email could not be sent.
notfallkontakte.ergebnis.grenze: Deleted. The notice is skipped – enough emails to emergency contacts have been sent today.
notfallblatt.passiert.text: Ablago doesn’t start any more, the device is broken, you can’t get in any more or someone else has to take over? The help page says step by step what to do.
notfallblatt.passiert.qr: Scan with your phone, read there and work on the computer.
notfallblatt.passiert.handbuch: The detailed instructions for restoring are in the administrator manual.
notfallblatt.ui.text: One A4 page with everything you need after a failure: the key for typing in with its fingerprint, the library ID, where the backups are, the link to the help page “Something happened?” with a QR code, and the emergency code in case you lock yourself out. Every new sheet has a new emergency code – the previous one then no longer works. The key is in no backup – keep the sheet in a password safe or printed in a safe place, separate from the device running Ablago.
notfallblatt.notfallcode.text: Can’t get in with any account? In the home network, open this address and enter the emergency code.
notfallblatt.notfallcode.ohne-adresse: Can’t get in with any account? In the home network, open your library’s address with /notfall at the end.
notfallblatt.notfallcode.hinweis: Works once – afterwards you print a new emergency sheet. The key above never belongs in the browser.
notfallzugang.text: Anyone who has locked themselves out gets back in with the emergency code from the emergency sheet via Ablago’s address with /notfall at the end, and sets a new password for an account with administration rights. The code works once; every new emergency sheet brings a new one.
notfallzugang.code: Valid emergency code: on the emergency sheet of {datum}.
notfallzugang.code.keiner: There is no valid emergency code right now. Download an emergency sheet under Encryption – it has a new one.
notfallzugang.internet: Allow emergency access from the internet
notfallzugang.internet.hilfe: Default: only from the home network. It then also works from the internet – for everyone who knows the address and has the code.
notfallzugang.internet.warnung: The emergency access can be reached from the internet. Whoever finds your emergency sheet can get into your library from anywhere with it. Only allow this if you have to reach Ablago without the home network.
notfallzugang.nicht-heimnetz: You aren’t opening Ablago from the home network right now. The emergency access wouldn’t work from here.
notfallzugang.grund.oeffentlich: Ablago sees your address as {code}. If you open Ablago at home via its public name, the request goes via the internet. A local DNS entry that points the name straight to the proxy at home helps.{hilfe}
notfallzugang.grund.proxy: Ablago sees your address as {code}. Your proxy passes the address on in a way Ablago can’t trust. More under “What the proxy tells Ablago”.{hilfe}
notfallzugang.grund.gateway: Ablago sees your address as {code}. That is the gateway address of its own network, with Docker the one of the Docker network. With it, Ablago can’t tell the home network from the internet, so the request counts as not from the home network. Remedy: a port mapping without the userland proxy, a reverse proxy with X-Forwarded-For, or an address of its own for the container (macvlan).{hilfe}
notfallzugang.frage: Allow emergency access from the internet?
notfallzugang.frage.text: Then anyone with your emergency sheet gets into your library from anywhere, not only from the home network. Everyone who administers gets an email each time it is used.
verschluesselung.schluessel-erzeugt-pass: Key created. Passwords can be stored now.
verschluesselung.alle-gespeicherten-pass:
All stored passwords and secrets (see “What is encrypted”) are encrypted with a new key – all or nothing. Afterwards you need a new emergency sheet.

Older backups stay encrypted with the previous key: keep the old emergency sheet as long as you need them.
verschluesselung.passwoerter-und-andere-: Ablago stores passwords and other secrets encrypted – sending email, mailboxes, sign-in via a provider, two-factor, package settings, password fields in folders; which ones they currently are is listed below under “What is encrypted”. It keeps the key in a file of its own, never in the database.
verschluesselung.nicht-feststellbar-laeu: can’t be determined (not running in a container)
verschluesselung.noch-kein-schluessel-so: No key yet. As long as it’s missing, no passwords can be stored (sending email, mailboxes, password fields).
verschluesselung.der-schluessel-mit-dem: The key with the fingerprint {span} is missing.
verschluesselung.liegt-die-datei-noch: {b} If the file is still in a backup, put it back under {span} and restart Ablago – then all passwords are readable again.
verschluesselung.erzeugst-du-stattdessen: If you create a new key instead, the passwords stored so far are lost and must be entered again (list below).
verschluesselung.unter-liegt-ein-anderer: Under {span} there is a different key ({span2}) from the one the passwords are encrypted with ({span3}). Put the right file there and restart Ablago. If it’s lost, remove the wrong file, restart and create a new key here.
verschluesselung.der-ordner-ist-kein: The folder {span} isn’t a volume of its own. In docker-compose.yml under {span2} add e.g. {span3}, otherwise the key is lost at the next update.
verschluesselung.sichere-die-schluesseld: Back up the key file separately from the database.
verschluesselung.eine-datenbanksicherung: {b} A database backup can only be fully restored with this key; without it the passwords in it can’t be read. If both are kept together, encryption doesn’t protect the backup.
verschluesselung.die-bisher-gespeicherte: The passwords stored so far become unreadable for good.
verschluesselung.wenn-der-schluessel-bek: If the key may have become known – say because a printed emergency sheet got lost – or you want to renew it regularly. All passwords and secrets (see “What is encrypted”) are encrypted with a new key, all or nothing; if something fails, the previous one stays in force. The old key isn’t kept.
verschluesselung.waren-schon-vorher-nich: ; {unlesbar} were already unreadable before and stay so
verschluesselung.das-neue-notfallblatt-h: Download the new emergency sheet and keep it safe. {link}
verschluesselung.eine-neue-sicherung-anl: Create a new backup – it’s encrypted with the new key.
verschluesselung.sicherung-laeuft-den-st: Backup running – you see the status under Backup.
verschluesselung.aeltere-sicherungen-sin: One older backup is still encrypted with the old key. Keep the old emergency sheet as long as you need it – or delete it under {link}.
{anzahl} older backups are still encrypted with the old key. Keep the old emergency sheet as long as you need them – or delete them under {link}.
verschluesselung.alles-hier-verschluesse: Ablago encrypts everything here with this key and takes it along when the key changes. It encrypts the backups with a key derived from it.
verschluesselung.mit-dem-vorhandenen-sch: can’t be read with the existing key – see below
verschluesselung.keine-alle-gespeicherte: None – all stored passwords and secrets can be read with the existing key.
